The fallback tint (no backdrop-filter, or prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) is opaque enough to hold text contrast.
Keyboard focus centres the specular highlight and swells the displacement the same as pointer hover.

components.name: Reflective Card

components.rationale: keep: Tier 1, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

The CSS forces text colour through --genui-reflective-card-ink (default #111), so an author can flip it to #fff on a dark tone and keep contrast.

Keyboard focus (:focus-visible / :focus-within) plays the same band shift as hover, so the state is not mouse-only.

components.name: Accordion Gallery

components.rationale: keep: Tier 1, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

a11y: Panels are list items and the links are the focus targets, so :focus-within expands the panel under keyboard focus.
Labels are real text and stay in the DOM, so screen readers read them even when the panel is collapsed.
The label sits on a gradient scrim with >= 4.5:1 contrast against white text.
The host's own focus outline is untouched.

components.name: Scroll Reveal

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Quiet editorial type reveal on scroll

components.rationale: keep: Tier 1, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

mode.description: scrub follows scroll position both ways; once reveals on entry with a word stagger.

end.description: Viewport fraction where scrub progress is 1.

stagger.description: Per-word delay in ms, once mode.

a11y: The word-split copy is aria-hidden; a visually hidden __sr span carries the original text once, in full.
Links and other inline elements inside the block are kept in the visual copy and stay focusable there; the sr copy is plain text, so they are not duplicated in the tab order.
At baseOpacity the dim pre-state is a deliberate design choice; once a word is fully revealed, contrast is the author's own.
Reduced motion skips the word split entirely, so the block reads at full opacity with no blur from the start and no scroll listener is attached.

a11y: The original text is kept once, in a visually hidden span read by screen readers; the split copy is aria-hidden.
No aria-label is added to the host; its heading level and role are unchanged.
With JS off, the author's plain heading shows, with no split and no hidden state.

components.name: Masked Heading

Group lines by measured layout, or split only on

The animated .__visual copy is aria-hidden and duplicates nothing in the reading order.
Each .__line keeps a small padding-bottom so its clipping box never cuts a descender.
The reveal plays once on entry; nothing changes on hover or keyboard focus.

components.name: Scroll-Locked Video Hero

source.description: Video hero scrubbed by scroll position

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from component-specs.md §9 prose only; no 21st.dev source was fetched or read.

poster.description: Solid background colour behind the canvas scene and shown while media is idle.

a11y: The overlay is real text in DOM order, not painted into the media.
The media (video or built-in canvas) is decorative: aria-hidden and stripped of controls; supply an aria-label on your own <video> for meaningful content instead.
The overlay sits on a scrim/text-shadow for at least 4.5:1 contrast against the media.
Nothing traps scroll or keyboard focus; the sticky stage releases normally once the track ends.
prefers-reduced-motion removes the pin and scrub entirely: the media holds one frame and the overlay is fully visible with no fade or lift.

components.name: Chroma Grid

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Grid with a spotlight following the cursor. Props: radius, columns, rows, damping

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

fadeOut.description: Spotlight fade-out (and fade-in) duration on pointer/focus leave, in ms.

a11y: Items can be links or buttons; :focus-visible shows the accent border and moves the spotlight to that card's centre, so keyboard users get colour too.
The desat and fade overlays are aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, so they never intercept clicks or reach the accessibility tree.
Titles sit on a scrim with contrast of at least 4.5:1 even while the card is grayscale.
Reduced motion drops the pointer-tracked spotlight entirely; the grid shows in colour and only the CSS hover/focus border remains.

components.name: Decay Card

source.name: react-bits
source.description: SVG turbulence displacement over an image. Grayscale by default

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

sensitivity.description: Multiplies pointer travel distance into displacement.

a11y: The media is decorative unless the author gives it role="img" and aria-label.
The caption is real text in the DOM, not injected by mount().
Keyboard focus gives the colour state through :focus-within without triggering the warp.
The SVG filter defs are aria-hidden and never in the tab order.

components.name: Ripple Distortion

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Water-ripple displacement over an image

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

a11y: The duplicated `__warp` layer is `aria-hidden`; only the original `__media` element carries any label or alt text.
With `trigger:"move"` no click is listened for, so clicks are never intercepted.
With `trigger:"click"` the host is not made focusable: the effect is decoration only, and the host's own interactivity (or lack of it) is unchanged.
Reduced motion skips duplicating the media entirely: the image stays static and no filter or listener is attached.

components.name: Masonry

hoverLift.description: Lift the hovered or focused item slightly.

a11y: Reading order is DOM order, which matches the visual column order.
Items that are links keep a visible :focus-visible ring; the hover/focus lift transform does not clip it.
Captions are real text and stay in the DOM at every breakpoint.

components.name: Shiny Text

source.name: react-bits

disabled.description: Show a plain solid colour with no shimmer.

a11y: The text is never split into spans; screen readers read it once, normally.
The base colour must pass 4.5:1 against the background on its own, since the band only briefly raises local contrast.
Reduced motion keeps the band fixed at 50%, so the surface still reads as metallic but does not move.
Forced-colors mode drops the gradient and paints the text in CanvasText.

components.name: Spotlight Card

source.name: react-bits

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

a11y: The spotlight and border-ring layers are decorative pseudo-elements, so they are not in the accessibility tree.
:focus-within shows the same centred glow as pointer hover, so keyboard users get equivalent feedback.
The host's own focus outline is untouched by the pseudo-element layers.
The default colour's alpha (0.12) keeps card text contrast; a custom colour should stay at or below roughly 0.2 alpha for the same reason.

components.name: Tilted Card

glare.description: Brighten the edge closest to the viewer.

a11y: Content order is unchanged; mount only wraps the existing children in .genui-tilted-card__inner.
If the host is focusable, keyboard focus gives the same static lift (scale) as pointer hover, with no directional tilt.
The caption is not the only way to get its information: the same text is also given through a visually hidden element linked with aria-describedby.
The glare and caption bubble are aria-hidden, decorative layers; they never enter the accessibility tree.
glareOpacity keeps a sane default cap so the glare layer does not wash out host text contrast.

components.name: Stack

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Physical card stack, sendToBackOnClick

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

sendToBackOnClick.description: Click, Enter or Space on the top card also sends it to the back.

a11y: The host is role="list" and each card role="listitem"; only the top card is in the tab order, with role="button" and an aria-label ("Send card to back", overridable with data-genui-stack-label).
After a reorder, focus moves to the new top card and a visually-hidden aria-live="polite" region announces which card it is.
Reordering moves DOM nodes rather than repainting, so reading order always matches the pile order.
Card content is real text, not an image or canvas.

components.name: Card Swap

source.name: react-bits
source.description: 3D card swap. Props: cardDistance, skewAmount, elastic easing

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (port-with-attribution)

skewAmount.description: Skew per depth slot, in deg.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause the cycle while the pointer is over the stack (keyboard focus always pauses it).

a11y: Auto-rotation pauses on pointer hover (when pauseOnHover is set) and always on keyboard focus inside the stack, per WCAG 2.2.2.
A visually hidden 'Next card' button gives manual, non-time-based control and becomes visible on keyboard focus.
Cards stay in DOM order; only their --genui-card-swap-slot custom property changes, so no focus or reading-order surprises come from a swap.
Reduced motion turns off the auto-cycle entirely; the Next button still reorders the cards, instantly.

components.name: Scroll Choreography

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Four images choreograph, one hero expands full-screen

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (clean-room); no-license but effect (multi-image scroll choreography that expands one panel) is a generic, reimplementable scroll technique, not brand-specific

captionAt.description: Track progress (0-1) at which the caption starts fading in.

smoothing.description: rAF lerp factor applied to the scroll progress each frame.

a11y: The four images are decorative unless the author labels them; the DOM order never changes, so reading order is unaffected by the visual scale and drift.
The caption is real text in normal flow, on a gradient scrim over the hero for >=4.5:1 contrast.
Nothing traps scroll or keyboard focus; the pin releases once the track ends and the page scrolls on normally.
A host without exactly 4 ".genui-scroll-choreography__item" children logs a console warning and mount is a no-op, so a malformed demo never leaves the section pinned or hidden.

components.name: Glyph Portal

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Scroll through a letter into the next section. Reduced-motion built in

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the component-specs.md behaviour description only; no 21st.dev source was fetched or read, so no MIT attribution is owed (the upstream author is not recorded in the seed). Same treatment as liquid-glass-card.

origin.description: Fraction of the glyph box the scale grows from.

a11y: The cover SVG is aria-hidden and pointer-events:none at all times, so it never intercepts clicks or enters the accessibility tree.
The 'next' content stays in normal DOM order and reading order behind the cover.
Nothing traps focus: focus landing in the content while it is still covered scrolls the track to its end so the focused element is visible.
The glyph is decoration only; it carries no text alternative and none is needed.

components.name: Handwriting SVG

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Text drawn as handwritten strokes

components.rationale: keep: Tier 2, licence is portable (clean-room); no-license but 'text drawn as handwritten strokes' is a generic SVG stroke-draw text technique

mode.description: paths: author-supplied single-stroke <path> children. text: draws an aria-hidden outline copy of the host's own text.

duration.description: Total draw duration, in ms, split across the strokes in proportion to their length.

stagger.description: Delay between each stroke's start, in ms.

fillAfter.description: Fade a solid fill in once the last stroke finishes drawing.

a11y: In paths mode, mount adds role="img" to the host SVG when it is missing and logs a console warning when there is no aria-label, since the drawn strokes carry no text alternative on their own.
In text mode, the original text stays in the DOM as visually hidden real text (.genui-handwriting-svg__sr) and the drawn SVG copy is aria-hidden, so screen readers read the phrase once, not twice.
The drawing plays once, never loops and traps no focus; nothing in the effect is interactive.
Stroke and fill colour contrast against the background is the author's own responsibility.

components.name: Circular Gallery

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Curved scrolling gallery with image bending

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no React Bits source was read, and the ogl/WebGL dependency is replaced by per-item DOM transforms on a circular arc plus a CSS perspective bend, so it ships dependency-free.

bend.description: Tilt, in degrees, of an item at the host's edge; 0 is flat, negative curves upward.

speed.description: Auto-scroll speed in px per second; 0 disables the drift, negative reverses it.

draggable.description: Let the pointer drag the strip.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause the drift while the pointer or focus is inside.

a11y: Items stay real list items in DOM order with their own links and captions; nothing is cloned, so screen readers read each item once.
Keyboard users Tab through the item links; a focused item is brought to the centre, the drift pauses while focus is inside, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight step one item.
Only horizontal wheel input (or Shift+wheel) moves the strip, so vertical page scrolling is never hijacked, and a real drag suppresses the trailing link click.
Reduced motion leaves a plain horizontal scroll-snap strip with no arc, drift, rAF loop or bend.

components.name: Flying Posters

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Vertical poster gallery, 3D distortion on scroll

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read, and the WebGL (ogl) original is replaced by native scrolling plus CSS 3D transforms driven by custom properties, so it ships with no dependency.

speed.description: Autoplay drift, in px per second; 0 turns autoplay off.

bend.description: Extra bend from scroll velocity, in degrees.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause autoplay while the pointer or focus is inside the gallery.

a11y: The gallery is a native scroll container, so wheel, touch, scrollbar and keyboard scrolling (with tabindex="0" on the host) all work unchanged.
Loop copies of the posters are aria-hidden and inert, so screen readers and the Tab order meet each poster exactly once.
Autoplay pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is inside the gallery and for a moment after any wheel or touch scroll.
Reduced motion removes the copies, the autoplay and every transform: the posters become a plain, flat scrolling list.

components.name: Dome Gallery

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Drag-to-explore 3D dome. CAUTION: drag fights scroll on mobile

components.rationale: Clean-room CSS 3D implementation from the one-line effect description only; no React Bits source was read, no WebGL or gesture library is needed, and touch-action: pan-y keeps vertical page scroll working on mobile.

rows.description: Rows of tiles stacked up the dome.

Moving focus onto a link or button inside a tile turns the dome to face that tile, so the focused element is always on screen.
Tiles facing away from the viewer only fade out (opacity and pointer-events), so their content stays in the accessibility tree and in DOM tab order.
Reduced motion never builds the dome: the tiles stay in a flat, horizontally scrollable strip with no drift, inertia or 3D transforms.

components.name: Fluid Glass

source.name: react-bits
source.description: WebGL glass lens. Modes: lens, bar, cube

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; a single raw-WebGL fragment shader replaces the three.js scene, so the lens, bar and cube modes ship dependency-free within budget.

a11y: The WebGL canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's own text and controls stay in DOM order above it and are never copied.
The backdrop stays dark (under 60% of the accent colours) so light text on the card keeps its contrast wherever the glass passes.
Reduced motion stops the render loop and draws one still frame with the glass centred; the CSS stand-in stops drifting too.
Without WebGL or script a static CSS gradient and glass shape stand in, and forced-colors mode hides the decoration entirely.

components.name: Metallic Paint

Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback sheen and shows one still frame of the metal.
Forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText with a visible border.

components.name: Silk

Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback drift and shows one still frame of the fabric.

components.name: Grainient

components.name: Iridescence

The pointer only moves a highlight; no information or action depends on it, and no click or key is intercepted.

components.name: Text Scroll Animation

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Type animates on scroll. CAUTION: Lenis hijacks native scrolling

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read, and the smooth-scroll dependency was dropped so native scrolling is never hijacked.

baseOpacity.description: Opacity of a character before it animates in.

rise.description: Starting vertical offset of a character, any CSS length.

a11y: The per-character copy is aria-hidden; a visually hidden span carries the original text once, so screen readers read whole words, not letters.
Scrolling is never intercepted or smoothed: the effect only reads native scroll position through a passive listener.
The host keeps its element, heading level and role; with JS off the plain authored text shows at full opacity.
Reduced motion skips the split and the scroll listener entirely, and a live switch to reduce snaps every character to its final, fully legible state.

Meant for brand marks and wordmarks, not over product photography.

The shader layer is clipped to the logo's own shapes, so its footprint and legibility are the same as the plain logo's.
Reduced motion draws one still frame and runs no animation loop; a live change of the preference stops or resumes the loop.

The surface mixes bright and dark regions, so text on it should carry a shadow or scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo does this).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop, the pointer pull and the fallback drift and shows one still frame; forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText.

components.name: Model Viewer

source.name: react-bits
source.description: 3D model viewer - 360 product rotation

components.rationale: Clean-room CSS 3D implementation from the effect description only: a procedural faceted product (or author-supplied inline CSS 3D/SVG markup) turns 360 degrees with drag and keyboard control, with no three.js, no model files and no external assets.
components.tierNote: PARKED - needs 3D assets; 61.2% of products have only 1 image

components.name: Water Ripple Image

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Water ripples over any image

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; click-driven concentric rings with a refraction read make it distinct from ripple-distortion's pointer-move noise, and masked clones replace WebGL so it ships dependency-free on any media.

radius.description: Radius a ring reaches by the end of its life, in px.

autoDrip.description: Drop at a random spot every this many ms while on screen; 0 turns it off.

a11y: Every ring is an aria-hidden, inert clone of the media with its ids stripped, so screen readers meet the image's label once and no cloned link or control can take focus.
Rings ignore pointer events and nothing calls preventDefault, so a click still reaches any link or control inside the host.
The host is not made focusable: the ripple is decoration only and never carries information.
Reduced motion (at mount or changed live) clears every ring, stops the loop and ignores clicks; forced-colors mode hides the rings.

components.name: 3D Testimonials

source.description: Infinite-loop scroller for text, images or video

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no 21st.dev source was fetched or read, so no MIT attribution is owed. A tilted, endlessly looping testimonial wall is a common social-proof section and costs no dependency: CSS keyframes do the motion and the script only adds the seamless-loop copies.

Hover and keyboard focus inside the wall pause the loop (pauseOnHover), so a quote can be read to the end.
The loop pauses while the host is off screen, and reduced motion removes the copies and stops the rows; each row then scrolls by hand.
Forced-colors mode draws each card with a CanvasText border on Canvas.

components.name: Animated Testimonials

source.description: 3D rotating images, word-by-word text

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line behaviour description only; no 21st.dev source was fetched or read, so no MIT attribution is owed, and framer-motion is replaced by CSS keyframes plus a few lines of dependency-free script.

autoplay.description: Step to the next testimonial on a timer.

pauseOnHover.description: Pause autoplay while the pointer is over the component; keyboard focus always pauses it.

Inactive testimonials are visibility:hidden, so screen readers and the tab order only reach the one on show.
Previous and Next are real buttons with aria-labels; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight also step while focus is inside, and manual steps are announced through a polite live region.
Autoplay pauses on hover, on keyboard focus, in a hidden tab and off-screen; reduced motion turns autoplay, the portrait swing and the word reveal off entirely.

components.name: AI Chat Input

source.name: 21st.dev
source.description: Agentic chat input with spring physics

components.rationale: keep: AI chat input is core to AG-UI, kept regardless of tier label; license unknown but 'agentic chat input with spring physics' is a generic UI pattern (chat input box), not a distinctive branded design

placeholders.description: Placeholder strings the field cycles through while empty and unfocused.

submitOnEnter.description: Enter submits; Shift+Enter always inserts a newline instead.

a11y: The field requires a real `<label>` from the host, visible or visually hidden; the placeholder is never the field's only label.
The send button has `aria-label="Send"`, which switches to `"Stop"` together with `aria-busy="true"` while busy.
Suggestion chips are real `<button>`s, reachable and activatable by keyboard.
A visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` status region announces "Sending…" while busy.
Focus rings are visible on the field, send button and chips; the default theme keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast.
Enter submits and Shift+Enter inserts a newline; IME composition (`isComposing`) is respected so composing text never submits early.

components.name: True Focus

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Focus-pull across words

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only (no React Bits source read): a dependency-free word-by-word focus pull with a gliding corner frame, useful for hero taglines and section headings.

blur.description: Blur on the words out of focus, in px.

dim.description: Opacity of the words out of focus.

pause.description: Time each word holds focus before the next pull, in ms.

glowColor.description: Colour of the glow around the frame.

manual.description: Hover drives the focus instead of the timer; the resting state is fully sharp.

a11y: The original child nodes move unchanged into a visually hidden span, so screen readers read the text once with its inline markup; the split word copy and the frame are aria-hidden.
The host keeps its element, heading level and role; no aria-label or tabindex is added.
With manual set, the resting state is fully sharp, so keyboard and touch users who never hover see every word clearly.
Reduced motion and forced-colors mode remove the blur and dimming entirely, and reduced motion also hides the frame and stops the timer.

components.name: Particle Text

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Type dissolves into particles

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read. A dependency-free 2D canvas samples the host's own laid-out text, so the effect needs no library and the real text stays in the DOM.

gap.description: Sampling step in px; smaller is denser (capped at 6000 particles).

color.description: Particle colour; empty uses the host's text colour.

accent.description: Second colour blended across the width; empty means a single colour.

spread.description: How far dissolved particles drift, in px.

duration.description: Length of one dissolve and of one reassembly, in ms.

hold.description: How long the letters hold before dissolving, in ms.

loop.description: Dissolve and reassemble on a loop; off keeps the letters formed.

repel.description: Pointer scatter radius in px; 0 disables it.

a11y: The original text is never moved or split: it stays in the DOM once, read normally by screen readers, selectable and findable; only its paint is made transparent.
The particle canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree and never blocks clicks or selection.
The text is painted transparent only after particles exist; with no 2D canvas, no script or a failed sample, the plain text shows.
Reduced motion and forced-colors mode remove the canvas and show the plain text.

components.name: Split Flap Text

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Airport departure-board flip

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only ("Airport departure-board flip"); no upstream source or docs were read, and it ships as dependency-free DOM tiles with CSS 3D flaps and one timer.

flips.description: Random characters each tile shows before it settles (each tile uses between half and all of them).

flipDuration.description: Duration of one flap turn, in ms.

stagger.description: Delay between neighbouring tiles starting, in ms.

charset.description: Characters the tiles cycle through on the way to their target.

uppercase.description: Show the board in capitals; the spoken text keeps its original case.

replayOnHover.description: Replay the flip when the pointer enters or the host receives focus.

loop.description: Replay the flip this many ms after it settles; 0 plays once.

a11y: The original text is kept once, in a visually hidden span that screen readers read; the tile board is aria-hidden, so the random intermediate characters are never announced.
The host keeps its element, role and heading level; no aria-label or live region is added.
Choose ink and tile colours that pass 4.5:1 against each other; the defaults (#f4efe2 on #1a1d24) are about 14:1.
Reduced motion shows the final characters on still tiles: no flips, timers or IntersectionObserver.

components.name: Warp Text

source.description: Type warped through a shader

from.description: Gradient start colour (left), as #rgb or #rrggbb; also used by the static fallback.

amplitude.description: Peak displacement of the warp, in CSS px.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

chroma.description: RGB split between the colour channels, in CSS px.

interactive.description: A soft lens bulge follows the pointer over the text.

a11y: The original text stays in the DOM exactly once, only made transparent while the shader draws, so screen readers, find-in-page, selection and translation all use the real words.
The warped canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; focus, links and reading order inside the host are unchanged.
Reduced motion hides the canvas, stops the render loop and shows the text as a still gradient fill.
Forced-colors mode drops the gradient and the canvas and paints the text in CanvasText.

components.name: Blur Text

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Type blurs into focus

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read, and the framer-motion dependency is replaced by one CSS keyframe animation staggered through custom properties.

replay.description: Blur the text out again when it leaves the viewport and replay on re-entry.

a11y: The original text is kept once, in a visually hidden span that screen readers read; the split, animated copy is aria-hidden.
The host's element, heading level and role are unchanged, and no aria-label is added.
Text is only hidden while an IntersectionObserver is present to reveal it; without one, or with JS off, the plain text shows at once.
Reduced motion skips the split entirely, and a preference change mid-reveal settles every piece to sharp, fully opaque text.

components.name: Stroke Text

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Outlined editorial headline

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read. An outlined display headline is a staple editorial treatment and costs almost nothing as pure CSS.

fillColor.description: Colour of solid words and of the hover fill.

fillOnHover.description: Fill the outline from the bottom up on hover or focus.

a11y: The text is never split or cloned; screen readers read the headline once, as written.
Outlined glyphs have little ink, so use it only at display sizes (about 32px and up) with a stroke colour that passes 3:1 against the background.
The hover fill also runs on :focus-within, so keyboard users get the same state as pointer users.
Forced-colors mode drops the outline and paints the text solid in CanvasText; reduced motion makes the hover fill instant.

components.name: Scroll Stack

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Cards stack as you scroll

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; sticky-positioned cards pile up natively as the page scrolls, and a small IO-gated scroll listener adds a scale-and-dim depth cue without the upstream smooth-scroll dependency.

top.description: Distance from the top of the scroll container where the first card pins, in px.

offset.description: Extra pin offset per card, in px, so a ledge of each earlier card stays visible.

gap.description: Scroll distance between cards before they stack, in px.

scaleStep.description: Scale lost per card stacked on top.

dim.description: Brightness lost per card stacked on top.

maxDepth.description: Maximum number of stacked cards that keep adding depth.

a11y: Cards stay in DOM order and nothing is cloned or aria-hidden, so screen readers read every card once, in sequence.
Scrolling is never hijacked or smoothed: wheel, touch, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling behave natively.
A card that holds keyboard focus (:focus-within) rises above the pile at full size and brightness, so a focused link or button is never covered.
Reduced motion keeps the plain sticky stacking but drops the scale and dim depth cue and attaches no scroll listener.

components.name: Depth Carousel

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Carousel with depth

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; a dependency-free 3D coverflow driven by CSS custom properties replaces the upstream motion library, and no upstream source was read.

Keyboard parity: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End on the carousel move the front item, focusing an item with Tab brings it to the front, and the Previous/Next buttons are real labelled <button> elements.
Autoplay is off by default; when set, it pauses on hover, on keyboard focus inside the carousel, in a hidden tab and off-screen (WCAG 2.2.2).
Reduced motion drops every transition and turns autoplay off; items snap to their new positions and all controls still work.

components.name: Staggered Menu

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Multi-layer menu entrance

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line description "Multi-layer menu entrance" only; no upstream source was read and the GSAP timeline is replaced by staggered CSS transitions driven by one open class.

The 01/02 index numbers are CSS generated content with empty alternative text, so link names stay "Work", "Services" and so on.

components.name: Card Nav

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Card-based navigation treatment

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; a menu bar that expands into staggered link cards, rebuilt with CSS transitions instead of GSAP so it ships dependency-free.

stagger.description: Delay between each card's entrance, in ms.

radius.description: Corner radius of the bar and cards.

closeOnOutside.description: Close when the pointer goes down outside the navigation.

Esc closes the open panel from anywhere inside the navigation and returns focus to the toggle.
The closed panel is visibility:hidden, so its links leave the tab order and the accessibility tree; without script the panel is always shown.
Every link and the toggle keep a visible :focus-visible ring, and forced-colors mode outlines each card.

components.name: Pill Nav

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Pill-shaped navigation treatment

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; a rounded link track with a springy sliding pill indicator that collapses to a dropdown on narrow hosts, rebuilt with CSS transitions instead of GSAP so it ships dependency-free.

When collapsed, the menu button is a native <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Esc closes the menu and returns focus to it, and the closed list is visibility:hidden so its links leave the tab order.
The list only collapses when a menu button exists to reopen it, and forced-colors mode paints the pill in Highlight.

components.name: Flowing Menu

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Flowing menu treatment

open.description: Start open when a toggle button is present.

The optional toggle is a real <button> whose aria-expanded tracks the list; Escape closes the list and returns focus to the toggle.
Reduced motion shows the band in place with a still marquee, and forced-colors mode paints it in Highlight and HighlightText.

components.name: Magic Bento

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Bento grid layout

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read, and the GSAP dependency is replaced by a CSS grid plus one rAF-batched pointer handler that writes custom properties.

components.name: Gradual Blur

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Progressive blur reveal

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line description "Progressive blur reveal" only; no React Bits source or docs were read. A stacked, masked backdrop-filter band that sharpens content as it scrolls out of the panel edge is a common, reusable scroll affordance.

Forced-colors mode removes the band entirely so focus rings and system colours are never obscured; reduced motion keeps the blur but makes the fade instant.

components.name: Halftone Reveal

source.description: Halftone dissolve reveal

Reduced motion creates no canvas and attaches no scroll listener, so the content is fully visible from the start; a live switch to reduce removes the screen at once.
Forced-colors mode and print hide the screen, so the content keeps system colours and prints in full.

components.name: Scroll Expand

source.name: react-bits
source.description: Element expands on scroll

components.rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no React Bits source was read. A dependency-free scroll-linked clip or scale that replaces framer-motion with one custom property driven by an IntersectionObserver-gated scroll listener.

from.description: Collapsed size as a fraction of the full box.

In clip mode the clipped margin is decorative and the text never rescales, so zoomed text keeps its size; keep essential copy away from the outer 11% of the box, which is clipped while collapsed.
Reduced motion removes the clip and scale entirely, shows the element fully open, and attaches no scroll listener.

components.name: Soft Aurora

source.description: Soft aurora wash - quiet base layer

colorA.description: First curtain colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback wash.

colorB.description: Second curtain colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback wash.
